claim: TSMC began volume production of its first-generation 7nm (N7) process in 2018, a year before its first EUV-based process (N7+) entered volume production; N7 was patterned with 193nm ArF immersion (DUV) lithography.
evidence: "In 2018, TSMC became the first foundry to start 7nm FinFET (N7) volume production." (TSMC 7nm page); "N7+, the industry's first commercially available Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology" (TSMC PR, 7 Oct 2019); "For N7, TSMC continued to use deep ultraviolet (DUV) 193 nm ArF Immersion lithography." (WikiChip)
notes: TSMC's own pages show N7 came before its first EUV process. That N7 used DUV explicitly rests on WikiChip (tier 3). Contradicts the BCG/SIA statement CLM-0399.

claim: TSMC describes its N7+ process, which was delivering customer products in high volume by October 2019, as the industry's first commercially available EUV lithography technology.
evidence: "TSMC ... today announced that its seven-nanometer plus (N7+), the industry's first commercially available Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology, is delivering customer products to market in high volume. The N7+ process with EUV technology is built on TSMC's successful 7nm node" (TSMC PR, Hsinchu, Oct 7, 2019)

claim: BCG/SIA's 2021 value-chain breakdown (2019 data) puts chip design at about 50% of semiconductor industry value added, 53% of industry R&D and 13% of industry capital expenditure.
evidence: Stage box: "Chip design 53% of industry R&D 13% of industry capex 50% of the value added" (p. 15); Exhibit 4 "The semiconductor value chain includes seven differentiated activities" (% of industry total, 2019; p. 13)

metric.name: Chip design share of semiconductor industry value added
metric.population: Semiconductor value chain value added (design, EDA/IP, equipment, materials, front end, back end)
metric.methodology: BCG analysis using Capital IQ company financial reports and Gartner total market sizes

notes: The same page's body text says '65% of the total industry R&D and 53% of the value added'. Only the stage-box and Exhibit 4 figures sum to about 100% across stages, so they are more defensible.

claim: SIA/BCG estimated that in 2022 Taiwan held about 69% and South Korea about 31% of global sub-10nm logic wafer fabrication capacity, with the United States at 0%.
evidence: Exhibit 6 "Global wafer fabrication capacity by technology category by region, 2022 (top) and 2032 Forecast (bottom) (%)", row Logic <10 nm, 2022: 69% / 31% / 0% (p. 14); text: "Advanced logic capacity will see a shift—from almost 100% distributed between South Korea and Taiwan in 2022" (p. 13)

metric.name: Taiwan share of global <10nm logic wafer capacity
metric.population: Logic wafer fabrication capacity below 10nm; fabs over 5K wspm and 8-inch or larger; excludes R&D fabs
metric.methodology: BCG analysis of Department of Commerce and SEMI data

notes: Percentages read from chart data labels in the PDF text layer. The region attribution (Taiwan 69, Korea 31) follows the chart layout and The Register's reading (theregister.com, 8 May 2024). The same exhibit forecasts Taiwan at 47% and the US at 28% in 2032.

claim: In September 2026 Intel Foundry and ASML said High-NA EUV continues to be used in high-volume manufacturing at Intel Foundry, with more than one million wafers processed to date across tool certification, R&D and volume production on select layers of a subset of Panther Lake processors.
evidence: "High NA continues to be used in high-volume manufacturing production at Intel Foundry today, with more than one million wafers processed to date across early tool certification and testing, research and development efforts, and volume production on select layers for a subset of Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 3 processors, code-named Panther Lake." (ASML PR, 8 Sep 2026)

metric.name: Cumulative wafers processed on High-NA EUV (Intel Foundry)
metric.population: Wafers processed on High NA at Intel Foundry incl. certification, R&D and volume production
